learningObjectives.title: A divided Germany in the Cold War

questions.q: The democratic government of Germany after 1919 was the:
questions.explain: The Weimar Republic governed Germany from 1919 until the Nazi takeover.

questions.q: Hitler and the Nazis came to power in Germany in:
questions.explain: Hitler became Chancellor in 1933 and established a dictatorship.

options: Propaganda, terror and the removal of democracy
questions.explain: The Nazi regime was a one-party totalitarian dictatorship.

questions.q: After its defeat in 1945, Germany was:
options: Divided into occupation zones, later East and West Germany
questions.explain: The Allies divided Germany; it split into West (FRG) and East (GDR).

questions.q: In 1948-49, the Soviet blockade of West Berlin was defeated by the:
questions.explain: The Western Allies supplied West Berlin by air until the blockade was lifted.

questions.q: West Germany (FRG) and East Germany (GDR) differed in that:
options: West Germany was capitalist and democratic; East Germany was communist
questions.explain: The two Germanys embodied the wider Cold War divide.

questions.q: The Berlin Wall was built in:
questions.explain: East Germany built the Wall in 1961 to stop people fleeing to the West.

questions.q: The Berlin Wall was built mainly to:
options: Stop East Germans escaping to the West
questions.explain: The Wall halted the mass movement of skilled workers to the West.

questions.q: West Germany experienced an 'economic miracle' after the war, meaning:
questions.explain: Aid (Marshall Plan) and reform drove West Germany's recovery.
The Wall's fall in 1989 signalled the collapse of communist control.
East and West Germany reunited in 1990 following the Wall's fall.

questions.q: A key factor in the fall of the Berlin Wall was:
options: Growing protest and reforms across the Eastern Bloc (and Soviet weakness)
A German invasion of the USSR
questions.explain: Reform (Gorbachev) and mass protest undermined communist regimes.

questions.q: The persecution of Jews under the Nazis included the 1935:
questions.explain: The Nuremberg Laws removed Jewish citizenship and rights.

questions.q: The Cold War rivalry was mainly between:
options: The USA and the USSR (and their blocs)
questions.explain: Divided Germany sat on the front line of US-Soviet rivalry.

questions.q: The reunification of Germany in 1990 symbolised:
options: The end of the Cold War division of Europe
The founding of the Weimar Republic
questions.explain: German reunification marked the collapse of the postwar divide.

questions.q: The Weimar Republic faced serious problems in the 1920s including:
questions.explain: Economic crises and extremist violence weakened Weimar democracy.
